subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and the action items we discussed around Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and streaming behavior so we can align on a proposal: 

1) Goals you stated
   - TTFT target: <= 150ms median for single-turn chat (95th <= 300ms) across your EU and US regions.
   - Sustained throughput: 400 qps for short prompt workloads during peak windows.
   - Concurrency: expected ~60 concurrent streaming connections for production service.
   - Streaming behavior: prefer SSE to start (simplicity for web clients), but websocket for mobile fallback. Chunk cadence target: ~150-250ms between chunks for perceived responsiveness.

2) Open questions we promised to confirm
   - Do the TTFT numbers apply to warm model instances only, or must they include cold-starts? (We assume warm for SLA; we can propose a cold-start credit.)
   - Typical prompt/response lengths and model family (you said average prompt 60 tokens, response 120 tokens; confirm if that holds across templates).
   - Any hard constraints on TLS termination or self-managed KMS for Private deployment?

3) Next steps
   - We will share a short proposal with: perf targets, recommended Serving config (batching, KV cache), and streaming delivery options (SSE vs WS) — target EOD Wed PT.
   - Your team to share example traffic profile + a sample prompt set (10-20 representative prompts) so we can run a focused benchmark.

I attached a brief outline of the proposal and a reference spec for SSE/WebSocket chunking cadence. If this matches your notes, I’ll circulate the formal SLO proposal and a mutual action plan.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-ttft-slo-proposal.pdf, sse-websocket-specs.docx
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Eng Eval <eng-eval@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- TTFT: Targets are for warm instances only. Cold-starts are allowable up to 2s but should be infrequent; we’ll accept a separate cold-start SLA.
- Throughput: 400 qps is correct for peak short prompts; we also see ~1200 qps for batched batch-processing jobs at night (not latency-sensitive).
- Concurrency: 60 concurrent streaming users is our baseline; we may need burst capacity to ~150 concurrent during promos.
- Streaming: Preference order is SSE (web dashboard) -> WebSocket (mobile). Chunk cadence: we want 100-200ms cadence for small incremental tokens, but willing to accept 250ms during heavy load.

Attached is a 10-prompt sample set and our traffic histogram for the past 30 days (see Eng Eval attachment).

On the TLS/KMS question — for now TLS termination is managed by Redwood (no custom KMS), but we will require private deployment with customer-managed KMS for production after pilot.

Can you include recommended configuration for: autoscaling thresholds, batching window (ms), and KV cache TTL in the proposal? Also please call out how Redwood handles fallback to smaller model variants if capacity constrained.

Best,
Sarah

--
Sarah Liu
Head of Platform Engineering, FinTechCo
sarah.liu@fintechco.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Appreciate the clarifications, Sarah — this is exactly what we need. Summary of updates coming into the proposal: 

- TTFT: we’ll propose a warm-instance 95th <= 250ms SLA with median <= 120-150ms depending on model family. Outside of SLA we’ll include cold-start guidance (we recommend pre-warmed pools for production).
- Throughput & concurrency: proposal will include a baseline dedicated pool sized for 400 qps with autoscale to handle 1200 qps batch windows and burst concurrency to 150 users.
- Streaming chunk cadence: recommend default 150ms cadence with adaptive throttling to 250ms under sustained saturation; fallback path via websocket kept.
- Config recommendations: batching window 20-40ms for short prompt workloads, dynamic batching based on latency SLOs; KV cache TTL 10-60s (depends on session reuse); autoscaling thresholds: 70% GPU utilization target to scale up.
- Model fallback: automatic routing to a lower-cost quantized variant when load is high; proposal will call out quality vs cost tradeoffs and safe rollout steps.

I attached a short SLO proposal PDF and the SSE/WebSocket chunking spec. If acceptable, I’ll book a technical review with Rishi and Vivek for Thursday to validate the performance numbers and run a short benchmark on a mirror dataset.

Proposed timing:
- Wed EOD: formal SLO proposal (attached)
- Thu 11:00 PT: 30m tech review + benchmark plan (Rishi/Vivek + your Eng Eval)
- Fri: initial benchmark run and result share

If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
